item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
571
ABPZ20 KNHC 250512
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Aug 24 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
east of Johnston Island, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several
hundred miles west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Depression Ten-E, located well
southwest of the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.

Central East Pacific:
A tropical wave located well to the south of southern Mexico is
producing a large area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
Environmental conditions appear favorable for development of this
system, and a tropical depression is expected to form by the end of
the week while it moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15
mph, well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression could form during the latter part of the week or early
this weekend while the system drifts generally north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

Well Offshore of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of Central America
late this week or this weekend. Environmental conditions could
support some gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression could form late this weekend or early next week while it
moves westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph well offshore
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Depression Ten-E are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...ISELLE MOVING NORTHWESTWARD AS A STRONG TROPICAL STORM...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.7N 119.9W
ABOUT 660 MI...1060 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 305 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was 
located near latitude 20.7 North, longitude 119.9 West. Iselle is 
moving toward the northwest near 15 mph (24 km/h). A turn toward the 
west-northwest and a slower forward speed is expected later today. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is expected over the next few days, and 
Iselle is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low by early 
Friday. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle are affecting the west coast of the
Baja California Peninsula, and will continue for a couple more days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 250843
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
200 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
The infrared satellite presentation of Iselle remains steady early 
this morning, featuring an established curved band with very cold 
cloud tops of -75C to -80C that wraps about halfway around the 
storm. Moderate westerly wind shear continues to impact the system. 
Earlier microwave imagery showed an established core north and east 
of the center, although the western portion of the circulation was 
less defined. An ASCAT-B pass from earlier tonight indicated maximum 
winds of 53-56 kt, along with slightly larger 34-kt wind radii in 
the northeast, southeast and northwest quadrants. Recent objective 
and subjective Dvorak intensity estimates range from 51-63 kt. Given 
the steady satellite presentation and ASCAT data, and after blending 
the subjective and objective intensity estimates, the initial 
intensity is maintained at 60 kt for this advisory. The ASCAT data 
also indicated that Iselle is located farther northwest and moving 
slightly faster than previously estimated.

The tropical storm is moving northwestward around 13 kt. A turn 
toward the west-northwest, accompanied by a slight decrease in 
forward speed, is expected later today as mid-level ridging 
currently centered over the southern United States strengthens and 
expands westward into the eastern Pacific. This general heading is 
expected to continue over the next several days. The latest NHC 
track forecast has been shifted slightly to the left and is faster 
than the previous advisory to account for the adjustment to the 
initial position. The forecast remains near the middle of the track 
guidance envelope and is closest to the Google DeepMind Ensemble 
Mean (GDMI).

Iselle is currently moving over warm waters near 28 C and remains 
within a relatively moist mid-level environment, and has likely 
reached its peak intensity. As the storm moves west-northwestward, 
progressively cooler waters, increasing dry mid-level air, continued 
westerly wind shear and increasingly unfavorable upper-level winds 
are expected to cause gradual weakening over the next several 
days. The latest NHC intensity forecast calls for Iselle to weaken 
to a tropical depression by 60 h, and a post-tropical remnant low by 
72 h. However, the ECMWF and GFS simulated satellite imagery suggest 
that Iselle could struggle to maintain organized deep convection 
before that time, raising the possibility that the cyclone could 
become post-tropical earlier than currently forecast. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS

 24H  26/0600Z 21.9N 123.2W   50 KT  60 MPH

item.title: Tropical Storm Julio Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 250851
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Julio Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
200 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
Convection has increased markedly near the tropical cyclone over the 
past several hours. Moderate north-northeasterly wind shear, 
enhanced by the close proximity of Tropical Storm Iselle to the 
northeast, is displacing the concentrated shower and thunderstorm 
activity to the south and west. An earlier ASCAT pass indicated 
winds of 35-40 kt wrapping around the southern and eastern sides of 
the system. The latest Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB was 
3.0/45 kt, while objective estimates range from 28-39 kt. Based on a 
blend of the available intensity estimates and the ASCAT wind data, 
the system has been upgraded to Tropical Storm Julio, with an 
initial intensity of 40 kt. 

Julio is moving toward the north-northeast over warm sea surface 
temperatures and within a favorable upper-level wind environment, 
which should support modest strengthening over the next 12 h or so. 
However, given the small size of the storm, Julio is expected to 
become increasingly influenced by the outer circulation of Iselle 
later tonight and ultimately be absorbed by Iselle by early 
Wednesday. 
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/0900Z 15.7N 119.8W   40 KT  45 MPH
 12H  25/1800Z 18.4N 119.6W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  26/0600Z...DISSIPATED
